layers.title: Daily true-colour Earth (VIIRS NOAA-20)
layers.provider: NASA GIBS (LANCE / EOSDIS)
layers.sensor: VIIRS (bands I1, M4, M3 corrected reflectance)
layers.resolution: 375 m (VIIRS I-band); served at GIBS Level 9
layers.license: NASA EOSDIS open data, no restrictions
layers.attribution: Imagery: NASA Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS), part of NASA ESDIS. Data: NASA LANCE, NOAA-20 VIIRS.
layers.description_simple: What the whole planet looked like on a given day, in natural colours. Good for spotting volcanic plumes, large floods and smoke.
layers.description_scientific: Daily global composite of VIIRS corrected reflectance (Rayleigh-corrected TOA, true-colour band combination) from swath L1B (VJ102IMG). Daytime ascending passes only.
layers.limitations: One image per day; clouds hide the surface; 375 m is too coarse for buildings or small landslides. Swath gaps near the equator. GetCapabilities lists internal date gaps (e.g. 2019-12-31/2020-01-02, 2022-01-12/2022-01-14) that return HTTP 404. Note the GIBS REST path order is {z}/{y}/{x} (TileMatrix/TileRow/TileCol); the template already uses that order. No daylight observation (polar night in winter) and gaps between orbits are shown transparent: the dark areas in the source JPEG carry no data.

legend.simple: Natural colours, similar to what the human eye would see from space. There is no colour scale: the picture itself is the information.
legend.scientific: True-colour composite of VIIRS corrected reflectance: red = band I1, green = band M4, blue = band M3. NASA GIBS publishes no colormap for this layer because it is imagery, not a mapped variable.

source.label: NASA Worldview layer description: Corrected Reflectance (True Color, VIIRS, NOAA-20)

legend.note: No colour key applies. NASA notes an occasional checkered pattern near the poles where several orbits overlap.

layers.title: Radar backscatter, Sentinel-1 (OPERA RTC-S1)
layers.provider: NASA JPL OPERA (data at ASF DAAC), tiles by NASA GIBS
layers.license: NASA EOSDIS open data; contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data
layers.attribution: Imagery: NASA GIBS. Data: NASA JPL OPERA RTC-S1 (ASF DAAC), contains modified Copernicus Sentinel-1 data.
layers.description_simple: A radar picture that sees through clouds and works at night. Vegetation looks green, built-up ground white or pink, and smooth surfaces such as calm water black.
layers.description_scientific: False-colour rendering of terrain-flattened gamma0 backscatter (OPERA_L2_RTC-S1_V1, CMR C2777436413-ASF). Each date shows only the Sentinel-1 swaths acquired that day.
layers.limitations: C-band, not NISAR L-band: less penetration into vegetation. The tile is an 8-bit visualization, not calibrated dB values. Spatial coverage follows the OPERA production footprint (not verified here) and the 12-day Sentinel-1 revisit; most dates show only a few swaths. Many internal date gaps in GetCapabilities.

classes.label: White / pink: urban and/or sparsely vegetated areas
Black: calm water, dry sand, frozen ground

legend.simple: A false-colour radar image: vegetation looks green, towns and sparsely vegetated land look white or pink, calm water, dry sand and frozen ground look black, and rough water looks purple or magenta.
legend.scientific: False-colour RGB of Sentinel-1 RTC backscatter: co-polarized VV (or HH) in the red and blue channels, cross-polarized VH (or HV) in green. NASA publishes no colormap or value scale for this layer; other land covers can look similar.

source.label: NASA Worldview layer description: OPERA RTC-S1 (False Color)

legend.note: Swatches illustrate the colour names used in the NASA description; they are not sampled from a colour table (this layer has none). NASA advises consulting auxiliary data, because other land covers can have a similar appearance.

layers.title: Fire and burn-scar false colour (VIIRS M11-I2-I1)
layers.provider: NASA GIBS (LANCE / EOSDIS)
layers.sensor: VIIRS (bands M11 2.25 um, I2 0.86 um, I1 0.64 um)
layers.license: NASA EOSDIS open data, no restrictions
layers.attribution: Imagery: NASA GIBS, part of NASA ESDIS. Data: NASA LANCE, NOAA-20 VIIRS.
layers.description_simple: A false-colour view where burn scars look deep or bright red and vegetation looks bright green.
layers.description_scientific: Shortwave-infrared / near-infrared / red composite. Burned surfaces have low NIR and higher SWIR reflectance; active flaming fronts can saturate M11.
layers.limitations: Not a fire-detection product: use thermal anomalies (FIRMS) or GOES Fire Temperature for active fire. 375-750 m pixels miss small fires. Clouds block the view. Date gaps exist (e.g. 2025-08-31/2025-09-02). No daylight observation (polar night in winter) and gaps between orbits are shown transparent: the dark areas in the source JPEG carry no data.

classes.label: Deep or bright red: burn scars
Very dark: liquid water on the ground
Bright turquoise: snow and ice; high ice clouds

legend.simple: A false-colour image: burn scars look deep or bright red, vegetation bright green, bare soil pinkish, water very dark, snow and ice turquoise, and low clouds white.
legend.scientific: Corrected reflectance composite with red = M11 (shortwave infrared), green = I2 (near infrared), blue = I1 (red visible). Burned areas reflect more in M11 and less in I2, so they turn red; vegetation reflects strongly in I2, so it turns green. No colormap: it is imagery.

source.label: NASA Worldview layer description: Corrected Reflectance (Bands M11-I2-I1, VIIRS, NOAA-20)

legend.note: Swatches illustrate the colour names used in the NASA description; they are not sampled from a colour table (this layer has none). The red of a burn scar varies with the vegetation burned, the residue and how complete the burn was.

layers.title: Fire temperature every 10 minutes (GOES-East ABI)
layers.provider: NASA GIBS (data NOAA)
layers.resolution: 2 km at nadir (ABI IR); GIBS Level 7
layers.license: NOAA / NASA open data, no restrictions
layers.attribution: Imagery: NASA GIBS. Data: NOAA GOES-East ABI.
layers.description_simple: A weather-satellite view of hot spots over the Americas, refreshed every 10 minutes. Very hot fires glow yellow to white.
layers.description_scientific: Fire Temperature RGB (ABI 3.9, 2.2 and 1.6 um channels) from the geostationary GOES-East disk. Highlights high-temperature sources day and night.
layers.limitations: {time} must be a full UTC timestamp on a 10-minute boundary (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:00Z), not a date. Rolling retention: GetCapabilities on 2026-11-14 listed only ~4 days (from 2026-11-10T02:10Z) with sub-hourly gaps. Americas/Atlantic disk only; 2 km pixels; sun glint and hot bare ground can mimic fire.

classes.label: Purples to pink: clear sky over land
Near black: clear sky over water, snow, or night

legend.simple: Fires go from red (warm) through orange and yellow to near white (very hot). Burn scars are maroon, clear land is purple to pink, water clouds are blue and ice clouds are green.
legend.scientific: Fire Temperature RGB from GOES-East ABI using the 3.9, 2.2 and 1.6 micrometre channels: cooler fires appear only at 3.9 um (red); more intense fires add signal at 2.2 and 1.6 um, moving the colour towards yellow and white. It is a qualitative RGB, not a temperature scale in kelvin.

source.label: NASA Worldview layer description: Fire Temperature (ABI, GOES-East)

legend.note: Swatches illustrate the colour names used in the NASA description; they are not sampled from a colour table (this layer has none). The colour guide is quoted from NASA; the underlying reference is the NOAA GOES-R Fire Temperature RGB Quick Guide.

layers.title: Vegetation disturbance alerts (OPERA DIST-ALERT, HLS)
layers.provider: NASA JPL OPERA (data at LP DAAC), tiles by NASA GIBS
layers.license: NASA EOSDIS open data; contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data
layers.attribution: Imagery: NASA GIBS. Data: NASA JPL OPERA DIST-ALERT-HLS (LP DAAC), built from USGS Landsat and Copernicus Sentinel-2 data.
layers.description_simple: Flags places where plants have recently been lost, for example after a fire, logging or clearing. Red means a confirmed loss of at least half of the vegetation cover.
layers.description_scientific: OPERA_L3_DIST-ALERT-HLS_V1 (CMR C2746980408-LPCLOUD): per-pixel vegetation cover loss relative to a multi-year baseline. Classes (GIBS colormap): 0 no disturbance; 1-3 first/provisional/confirmed <50% loss; 4-6 first/provisional/confirmed >=50% loss; 7-8 confirmed and finished.
layers.limitations: Disturbance is not the same as deforestation: fire, drought, harvest and flooding also trigger it. Optical, so cloud cover leaves gaps (the Amazon wet season especially). Each date only shows granules processed for that day. We saw intermittent HTTP 500 responses on some tiles and dates (e.g. 2026-06-20 and 2026-09-15 at z9-z11), so the client should retry.

legend.simple: Teal means a loss of vegetation seen only once so far, olive or orange means seen twice (provisional), and yellow or red means confirmed. Red is a confirmed loss of at least half the vegetation cover; grey means the disturbance has finished. Near-black means no disturbance.
legend.scientific: OPERA DIST-ALERT-HLS vegetation disturbance status, classes 0-8: confidence (first detection, provisional, confirmed) crossed with magnitude (< 50 % or >= 50 % vegetation cover loss), plus two "finished" classes. Colours are an exact class lookup from the NASA GIBS colormap OPERA_Vegetation_Disturbance_Status.
legend.note: Transparent = no data. "No disturbance" is drawn as opaque near-black (#121212), so observed areas without change look dark, not empty.

layers.title: Tree cover loss year 2001-2025 (Hansen / UMD GFC v1.13)
layers.provider: University of Maryland GLAD / Google (tiles on Google Cloud Storage)
layers.license: CC BY 4.0
layers.attribution: Source: Hansen/UMD/Google/USGS/NASA
layers.description_simple: Where trees were lost between 2001 and 2025. The colour shows the year the loss was detected.
layers.description_scientific: Global Forest Change 2000-2025 v1.13 'lossyear' layer: stand-replacement disturbance (canopy removal) at Landsat scale, rendered as an RGB colour ramp by year. Reference: Hansen et al. 2013, Science 342:850-853.
layers.limitations: This tile path is not listed on the GFC download page; it is the path used by the GLAD web viewer, so it could change without notice (v1.11 and v1.12 paths also still respond). Tiles are RGB only, with no legend or values. Gross loss includes fire, plantation harvest and storms, not only deforestation. The provider warns against pixel-count area estimates and notes inconsistencies before and after 2011/2013. z13 returns 404.

legend.simple: Yellow appears to mark the oldest tree cover loss and red the most recent, with black for no loss. UMD publishes no legend for this version of the tiles, so the year labels are our own reading of the tiles, not an official key.
legend.scientific: Year of gross forest cover loss (lossyear) drawn on a yellow-to-red ramp: the green channel falls linearly from equal-to-red (yellow, first loss year) to zero (red, last loss year), in 25 equal steps for 2001-2025. The official UMD/Google viewer legend gives yellow = start of the record, orange = intermediate, red = latest year, black = no loss, dark grey (#404040) = water or no data.

source.label: UMD/Google Global Forest Change viewer, "Forest Loss Year" layer legend

legend.note: The published legend belongs to the v1.7 tiles (2000-2019) served from the same tile path pattern; no legend is published for the v1.13 tiles. That the ramp now ends at 2025 was checked by comparing v1.7 and v1.13 tiles pixel by pixel (same colour step for the same pixel; pixels new in v1.13 use the six reddest steps), so the year labels are measured, not quoted. Black and dark grey are opaque. Colours get darker when zoomed out; the reason is not documented.

layers.title: Daily snow cover (MODIS Terra NDSI)
layers.provider: NASA GIBS (data NSIDC / LANCE)
layers.license: NASA EOSDIS open data, no restrictions
layers.attribution: Imagery: NASA GIBS. Data: MODIS/Terra Snow Cover MOD10_L2 (NSIDC DAAC / LANCE).
layers.description_simple: Where the ground is covered by snow on a given day.
layers.description_scientific: Normalized Difference Snow Index snow cover from MOD10_L2 (V061 standard, 6.1 NRT). Daytime swath product mapped daily.
layers.limitations: Optical: no retrievals under cloud or polar night. Snow under dense forest is underestimated. Terra is in an extended mission; record continuity relies on VIIRS successors. Some multi-day gaps in the record (see GetCapabilities).

legend.simple: Pale yellow means a weak snow signal, salmon pink a strong one and bright red the maximum. Where nothing is drawn there is no snow, or the ground could not be seen (cloud, night, water).
legend.scientific: MOD10_L2 NDSI snow cover, integer values 1-100, one colour per value from the NASA GIBS colormap MODIS_NDSI_Snow_Cover: pale yellow (1) shading to salmon (99), with 100 in pure red. Value 0 and all flag classes are transparent.
legend.note: Transparent = NDSI 0 (no snow), missing data, no decision, night, inland water, ocean, cloud, detector saturated, fill. The colormap gives no units for the 1-100 index.

layers.title: Sea ice concentration (GHRSST MUR L4)
layers.provider: NASA GIBS (data NASA JPL PO.DAAC, MUR v4.1)
layers.resolution: 0.01 degree analysis grid (the underlying sea-ice input is coarser; not verified)
layers.license: NASA EOSDIS open data, no restrictions
layers.attribution: Imagery: NASA GIBS. Data: GHRSST Level 4 MUR v4.1 (NASA JPL, PO.DAAC).
layers.description_simple: How much of the polar ocean is covered by floating sea ice each day.
layers.description_scientific: Sea-ice fraction field distributed with the MUR-JPL-L4-GLOB-v4.1 foundation SST analysis (CMR C1996881146-POCLOUD). Gap-free daily analysis.
layers.limitations: This is an analysis (interpolated), not a direct image. About a 2-day latency (latest on 2026-11-14 was 2026-11-12). Not suitable for individual floes or leads; SAR (NISAR, Sentinel-1) is needed for those. For climate-record sea-ice extent, prefer the NSIDC Sea Ice Index (not reachable from our network).

legend.simple: The colour shows how much of the sea surface is covered by ice: purple for a little, violet-blue for about a quarter, green for about half, yellow for three quarters, red for about 90 % and white for a fully ice-covered sea. Ice-free ocean is drawn almost black.
legend.scientific: Sea ice concentration (area fraction) 0-100 % from the GHRSST MUR L4 analysis, one colour per 1 % step in the NASA GIBS colormap GHRSST_Sea_Ice_Concentration.
legend.note: Transparent = no data. The 0-1 % class is drawn as opaque dark grey (#111111), so ice-free ocean appears almost black, not empty.

layers.title: Daytime land surface temperature (MODIS Terra)
layers.provider: NASA GIBS (data LP DAAC / LANCE)
layers.license: NASA EOSDIS open data, no restrictions
layers.attribution: Imagery: NASA GIBS. Data: MODIS/Terra LST/Emissivity MOD11_L2 (LP DAAC / LANCE).
layers.description_simple: How hot the ground surface was in the late morning, measured from its heat glow.
layers.description_scientific: Split-window land surface temperature from MOD11_L2 (around 10:30 local solar time, descending). Clear-sky only.
layers.limitations: Surface skin temperature, not air temperature. No data under cloud. 1 km pixels mix land-cover types. SAR is not a substitute: thermal IR is the correct observation.

legend.simple: Purple and blue are the coldest ground, green is around freezing (273 K is 0 degrees Celsius), yellow is warm (300 K is about 27 degrees Celsius) and orange to red is very hot ground.
legend.scientific: MODIS/Terra daytime land surface temperature in kelvin, coloured in 0.6 K steps from < 200 K to >= 350 K by the NASA GIBS colormap MODIS_Land_Surface_Temp.
legend.note: Transparent = no data (the colormap marks only the fill value as no data).

layers.title: Root-zone soil moisture (SMAP L4)
layers.provider: NASA GIBS (data NASA GMAO / NSIDC DAAC)
layers.license: NASA EOSDIS open data, no restrictions
layers.attribution: Imagery: NASA GIBS. Data: SMAP L4 Surface and Root Zone Soil Moisture Analysis Update SPL4SMAU V008 (NSIDC DAAC).
layers.description_simple: How wet the soil is down to about 1 metre: a model guided by satellite measurements. Useful for drought.
layers.description_scientific: SPL4SMAU (CMR C3480440639-NSIDC_CPRD) 12z instantaneous root-zone (0-100 cm) soil moisture from the GEOS land model with SMAP brightness-temperature assimilation.
layers.limitations: This is a model product (kind = model), not a direct observation. 9 km. About a 4-day latency. Several short gaps in 2026 (e.g. 2026-08-09/2026-08-16) per GetCapabilities.

legend.simple: Orange and yellow mean dry soil, green means moderately moist, and light blue to dark blue means wet soil. The very wettest soils are shown dark grey.
legend.scientific: SMAP L4 analysed root-zone soil moisture as a volume fraction (m3 of water per m3 of soil), coloured from 0.000 to >= 0.700 by the NASA GIBS colormap SMAP_Analyzed_Soil_Moisture.
legend.note: Transparent = no data.

layers.title: Flood water, 2-day composite (MODIS Terra + Aqua)
layers.provider: NASA GIBS (data NASA LANCE MCDWD)
layers.license: NASA EOSDIS open data, no restrictions
layers.attribution: Imagery: NASA GIBS. Data: MODIS/Aqua+Terra Global Flood Product MCDWD_L3_NRT (NASA LANCE).
layers.description_simple: Shows flood water (water where it is not normally present) as well as normal surface water, combining two days of observations to see past some clouds.
layers.description_scientific: MCDWD L3 NRT 2-day flood product: surface water from MODIS water detection, compared against a reference water mask to flag unusual water.
layers.limitations: Optical: persistent cloud during storms hides floods; SAR (NISAR, Sentinel-1/OPERA DSWx-S1) is better during events. Cloud shadow and terrain shadow can be misclassified as water. MODIS is near end of mission; a VIIRS equivalent (VIIRS_Combined_Flood_2-Day, from 2025-06-03) exists in GIBS.

legend.simple: Red is flood water, yellow is flooding that returns to the same place in many years, and cyan is water that is normally there. Grey means there was not enough data.
legend.scientific: MCDWD L3 NRT 2-day water product, classes 1 = surface water, 2 = recurring flood, 3 = flood, 255 = insufficient data, coloured by the NASA GIBS colormap MODIS_Flood. Water pixels are split using reference-water and recurring-flood layers.
legend.note: Transparent = no water, or no data. NASA states the recurring-flood class exists only from Release 1.1 (10 December 2025); in earlier dates such pixels are most likely shown as flood. Grey also covers mountain areas removed by the terrain filter.

layers.title: Surface water from radar (OPERA DSWx-S1)
layers.provider: NASA JPL OPERA (data at PO.DAAC), tiles by NASA GIBS
layers.license: NASA EOSDIS open data; contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data
layers.attribution: Imagery: NASA GIBS. Data: NASA JPL OPERA DSWx-S1 (PO.DAAC), contains modified Copernicus Sentinel-1 data.
layers.description_simple: Open water mapped by radar, so it works through clouds: useful during floods.
layers.description_scientific: OPERA_L3_DSWX-S1_V1 (CMR C2949811996-POCLOUD): water and no-water classification from RTC-S1 backscatter, drawn in GIBS as not water, open water, inundated vegetation and two masked classes (HAND, layover/shadow).
layers.limitations: C-band: misses water under dense canopy (L-band NISAR is better there). Wind-roughened water and dry sand can be misclassified. Coverage follows Sentinel-1 swaths, so each date shows only that day's acquisitions. Several date gaps in the record.

legend.simple: Blue is open water and green is flooded vegetation. White is land that was observed and is not water; grey areas were masked out and carry no answer.
legend.scientific: OPERA DSWx-S1 water classification: 0 = not water, 1 = open water, 3 = inundated vegetation, 250 = HAND masked, 251 = layover/shadow masked, coloured by the NASA GIBS colormap OPERA_Dynamic_Surface_Water_Extent_S1.
legend.note: Transparent = fill value (no data). "Not water" is opaque white, so each radar swath covers the basemap.

layers.title: Surface water occurrence 1984-2024 (JRC Global Surface Water v1.5)
layers.provider: European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC) / Google
layers.license: Copernicus Programme data, free of charge without restriction of use (per the JRC download page)
layers.attribution: Source: EC JRC/Google
layers.description_simple: How often each place was covered by water over four decades. Solid blue means almost always wet; faint red or pink means water was seen only rarely.
layers.description_scientific: Percentage of valid Landsat observations classified as water, 1984-2024 (GSW v1.5). Pekel et al. 2016, Nature 540:418-422, doi:10.1038/nature20584.
layers.limitations: RGB visualization tiles, for display not analysis. Static summary with no time slider. The v1.5 seasonality, monthly and yearly assets cover only 2022-2024 (merge with v1.4 for full history). z14 returns 404. Clouds and terrain shadow reduce valid observations in some regions.

legend.simple: Solid blue means water was there almost all the time. Purple means about half the time, and faint red or pink means water was seen only rarely. Places never seen as water are left empty.
legend.scientific: Surface water occurrence, 1-100 % of valid Landsat observations classified as water. Per the JRC Data Users Guide the symbology runs from #FF0000 at 1 % opacity (1 % occurrence) to #0000FF at 100 % opacity (100 % occurrence); in the tiles both hue and opacity change linearly with occurrence.

source.label: JRC Global Surface Water Data Users Guide (v2024), Occurrence symbology

legend.note: Tile opacity equals the occurrence value, so low values are nearly see-through and their apparent colour depends on the basemap underneath. Transparent = not water or no data. The 25, 50 and 75 % colours were read from the tiles and match a straight red-to-blue blend.

layers.title: Water gained and lost 1984-2024 (JRC GSW transitions)
layers.provider: European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC) / Google
layers.license: Copernicus Programme data, free of charge without restriction of use (per the JRC download page)
layers.attribution: Source: EC JRC/Google
layers.description_simple: Shows where new lakes or reservoirs appeared, where water disappeared, and where it became seasonal, between the first and last years of the record.
layers.description_scientific: Categorical transitions between first-year and last-year water class (permanent, seasonal, new, lost, seasonal-to-permanent, and so on) from the GSW v1.5 time series. The tiles use the colour-blind-safe (deuteranopia) palette published by JRC, which differs from the table in the Data Users Guide for several classes.
layers.limitations: Compares only the start and end of the record; intermediate changes are hidden. RGB display tiles only. Reservoir-filling and land-reclamation signals are robust; small or narrow channels below 30 m are not resolved.

legend.simple: Blue is water that stayed permanent. Green shades are new water, dark red and pink are water that was lost, and orange and yellow mark water that switched between seasonal and permanent. Grey is water that appeared and then disappeared again.
legend.scientific: JRC GSW transition classes 1-10 between the first and last year of the record. The tiles use the colour-blind-friendly (deuteranopia) symbology published by JRC (transitions_deuteranopia.qml); class names are those of the Data Users Guide.

source.label: JRC Global Surface Water symbology file: transitions_deuteranopia.qml

legend.note: Transparent = not water. Nine of the ten colours were confirmed by reading the tiles; "Ephemeral permanent" (#7f7f7f) did not occur in the tiles checked and is taken from the symbology file. The Data Users Guide table lists a slightly different standard palette (for example Lost permanent #D1102D), which these tiles do not use.

layers.title: Annual vegetation disturbance (OPERA DIST-ANN, HLS)
layers.provider: NASA JPL OPERA (data at LP DAAC), tiles by NASA GIBS
layers.license: NASA EOSDIS open data; contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data
layers.attribution: Imagery: NASA GIBS. Data: NASA JPL OPERA DIST-ANN-HLS (LP DAAC), built from USGS Landsat and Copernicus Sentinel-2 data.
layers.description_simple: A yearly summary of where vegetation was lost or damaged.
layers.description_scientific: OPERA_L3_DIST-ANN-HLS_V1 (CMR C2519119034-LPCLOUD): annual roll-up of DIST-ALERT vegetation-loss status. GetCapabilities lists annual values for 2023, 2024 and 2025.
layers.limitations: Same cause ambiguity as DIST-ALERT (fire, harvest and clearing are not separated). Annual granularity. The 2026 annual value was not yet published on 2026-11-14.

legend.simple: Yellow marks a confirmed loss of less than half the vegetation cover during the year, red a confirmed loss of half or more. Grey means the disturbance has finished; near-black means no disturbance.
legend.scientific: OPERA DIST-ANN-HLS annual summary of DIST-ALERT: only confirmed disturbances of the year are reported (status values 0, 3, 6, 7, 8). Colours are an exact class lookup from the NASA GIBS colormap OPERA_Vegetation_Disturbance_Annual.
legend.note: Transparent = no data. "No disturbance" is drawn as opaque near-black (#121212).

layers.title: Vegetation greenness, 16-day (MODIS Terra NDVI)
layers.provider: NASA GIBS (data LP DAAC)
layers.license: NASA EOSDIS open data, no restrictions
layers.attribution: Imagery: NASA GIBS. Data: MODIS/Terra Vegetation Indices 16-Day L3 Global 250m MOD13Q1 V061 (LP DAAC).
layers.description_simple: How green and leafy the land is, averaged over 16 days. It shows crops, droughts and seasons.
layers.description_scientific: MOD13Q1 V061 NDVI composite (best-quality pixel over 16 days).
layers.limitations: Valid {time} values are the composite start dates, which restart each 1 January (e.g. 2026-01-01, 2026-01-17 ... 2026-10-16). Use the GetCapabilities list; other dates are not guaranteed. Latency is about a month. NDVI saturates over dense forest.

legend.simple: Pale and brown tones mean little or no green vegetation, yellow-green means some, and dark green means dense, leafy vegetation.
legend.scientific: MOD13Q1 16-day NDVI (unitless), coloured from 0.0 to 1.0 by the NASA GIBS colormap MODIS_L3_NDVI. NDVI at or below zero is transparent.
legend.note: Transparent = NDVI at or below zero, or no data.

layers.title: Farmland and crop types 2021 (ESA WorldCereal)
layers.provider: ESA WorldCereal (VITO and partners), tiles by Terrascope (VITO)
layers.license: CC BY 4.0 (ESA WorldCereal 2021 products v100, Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.7875105)
layers.attribution: © ESA WorldCereal project 2021 (CC BY 4.0), tiles by Terrascope/VITO
layers.description_simple: Shows where crops were grown in 2021 and, by colour, whether a field grew maize, winter cereals, spring cereals or another crop. Rice, soybean and other crops are not told apart, and orchards, vineyards and pastures are not shown.
layers.description_scientific: Four ESA WorldCereal 2021 v100 products at 10 m, classified from Sentinel-1 (VV, VH) and Sentinel-2 time series per agro-ecological zone: the annual temporary-crop extent and, within it, the binary maize, winter-cereals and spring-cereals maps. This app requests each product in one colour and stacks them with the most specific on top; at zooms 0 to 3 it shows tiles pre-rendered from the service's zoom-3 tiles (reduced below zoom 3). Reported for the temporary-crop extent: user's accuracy 88.5 %, producer's accuracy 92.1 %; for crop type: 82.5 % overall agreement with a street-view reference set (Van Tricht et al. 2023, ESSD 15, 5491-5515).
layers.limitations: One year only, 2021. Only maize and cereals are distinguished, and cereals means wheat, barley and rye together, which the product does not separate. Rice, soybean, cotton, vegetables and all other temporary crops share one colour. Perennial crops (orchards, vineyards, plantations) and pastures are not mapped. Spring cereals were mapped only in parts of the Northern Hemisphere. Where a field grew a cereal and maize in the same year, only maize is shown. Neighbouring agro-ecological zones use different season definitions, so seams can appear between them. Reference data for checking crop types in 2021 were limited. Zoomed out to the whole world, a pixel is coloured when at least a quarter of the samples it covers are crops, so scattered farmland disappears and areas are not to scale: zoom in before judging extent.

legend.simple: Yellow is maize, orange-red is winter cereals, light blue is spring cereals, and green is any other temporary crop, for example rice, soybean, cotton or vegetables. Land with no colour had no temporary crop mapped in 2021, or was not covered by the map.
legend.scientific: Value 100 of each binary WorldCereal 2021 product, drawn in one colour per product and stacked: temporary-crop extent at the bottom, then spring cereals, winter cereals and maize on top. Cereals are the Triticeae wheat, barley and rye.

source.label: ESA WorldCereal: global maps 2021, product definitions

legend.note: The class meanings are WorldCereal's; the colours are chosen by this app (a colour-blind-safe set) and sent to the tile service with each request. Rice, soybean and other crops are not separate classes. Orchards, vineyards and other perennial crops, and pastures, are not shown.

layers.title: Built-up and settlement extent 2010 (HBASE, Landsat)
layers.provider: NASA SEDAC / CIESIN (Columbia University), tiles by NASA GIBS
layers.license: NASA SEDAC open data (CC BY 4.0 per SEDAC policy; not verified this session)
layers.attribution: Imagery: NASA GIBS. Data: Global Human Built-up And Settlement Extent (HBASE) v1, NASA SEDAC / CIESIN.
layers.description_simple: Where buildings and settlements were around 2010: a baseline to compare against today's imagery.
layers.description_scientific: HBASE v1 (CMR C3550193482-ESDIS): built-up and settlement extent from Landsat GLS 2010, drawn in GIBS as three classes (HBASE, road, not HBASE).
layers.limitations: A single epoch (circa 2010), so it shows no change by itself. Compare with recent Sentinel-2 or EOX annual mosaics or with NISAR backscatter. For multi-epoch built-up, GHSL (JRC) is the better source but no browser tile service was found (unverified).

legend.simple: Orange is built-up or settled land around 2010 and blue is roads. Light grey is land that is not built-up.
legend.scientific: HBASE v1 classification from Landsat GLS 2010: 200 = not HBASE, 201 = HBASE, 202 = road, coloured by the NASA GIBS colormap Landsat_Human_Built-up_And_Settlement_Extent.
legend.note: Transparent = no data, cloud or shadow. "Not HBASE" is opaque light grey, so the layer covers the basemap over all mapped land.

layers.title: Night lights, daily (VIIRS Day/Night Band, NOAA-20)
layers.provider: NASA GIBS (data NASA LANCE Black Marble)
layers.resolution: 15 arc-second grid (~500 m); DNB native ~750 m
layers.license: NASA EOSDIS open data, no restrictions
layers.attribution: Imagery: NASA GIBS. Data: NASA LANCE Black Marble VJ146A1 NRT (NOAA-20 VIIRS DNB).
layers.description_simple: Lights at night seen from space: cities, roads, gas flares and fishing fleets. Outages after disasters show up as missing lights.
layers.description_scientific: Daily gridded at-sensor DNB radiance (VJ146A1/VJ146A1G NRT, night descending passes).
layers.limitations: At-sensor radiance, not corrected for moonlight, clouds or atmosphere (the standard Black Marble VNP46A2 product does this). Summer twilight blanks high latitudes. Light is a proxy for activity, not a measurement of buildings or damage.

legend.simple: A greyscale picture: the brighter the pixel, the more light reached the satellite at night. Black is dark, white is the brightest light.
legend.scientific: Black Marble at-sensor top-of-atmosphere Day/Night Band radiance in nW/(cm2 sr), drawn in greyscale with a log10 stretch from 0 to >= 38.2 by the NASA GIBS colormap VIIRS_DayNightBand_At_Sensor_Radiance.
legend.note: Transparent = no data. Zero radiance is drawn as opaque near-black (#070707), so dark areas cover the basemap. Brightness is not only city light: NASA notes moonlit clouds, snow, sea ice, auroras, fires, gas flares and fishing fleets also appear.

layers.title: Cloud-free Sentinel-2 yearly mosaics 2017-2025 (EOX)
layers.provider: EOX IT Services GmbH
layers.license: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for non-commercial use; commercial use needs an EOX licence
layers.attribution: Sentinel-2 cloudless - https://cloudless.eox.at by EOX IT Services GmbH (Contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data <year>)
layers.description_simple: One cloud-free picture of Earth per year. Flip between years to watch cities, mines and new coastlines grow.
layers.description_scientific: Annual cloudless true-colour mosaics compiled from Sentinel-2 L1C/L2A scenes. Layer identifiers s2cloudless-2017_3857 ... s2cloudless-2025_3857 (2016 is 's2cloudless_3857').
layers.limitations: Substitute only the 4-digit year (YYYY) for {time}, not a full date. Mosaics blend many dates in each year, so they suit year-to-year change but not exact dating. Licence is non-commercial (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0). CORS echoes the request origin instead of '*'. Tested to z17 over Cairo; deeper zooms were not tested.

legend.simple: A colour picture of the land made from a year of Sentinel-2 images with the clouds removed. There is no colour scale: the picture itself is the information.
legend.scientific: Colour-corrected 8-bit RGB mosaic from Sentinel-2; EOX lists the RGB bands of its products as red = B04, green = B03, blue = B02. Colours are balanced for visual consistency, so they are not calibrated reflectance values.
legend.note: No colour key applies. EOX states the mosaics favour visual clarity and consistency over spectral accuracy.
